items.summary: A study by researchers at Clemson University and colleagues reveals that while AI chatbots effectively reject election conspiracy theories in text, they consistently generate convincing false images, audio, and video regarding voting fraud. The researchers tested popular models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Meta AI, finding that many failed to identify AI-generated media, even when created by themselves. Although some companies have improved safeguards, such as adding watermarks or refusing requests, others still produce deceptive content or fail to detect embedded origin data. The authors urge tech companies to treat election content as a sensitive category and enforce consistent guardrails across all model speeds to prevent the spread of disinformation before the US Midterms.
items.title: Study Finds AI Chatbots Still Generate Election Deepfakes

items.summary: Long John Silver's will permanently close its Woodlands outlet on Oct 31, following a string of recent closures in Singapore. The Jurong Point outlet shut on Oct 19, and at least four other locations closed earlier in 2026. Currently, the chain lists 11 outlets, down from 17 reported in July 2025. The brand is run by Zensho Food Singapore.
items.title: Long John Silver's Woodlands Outlet to Close Amid Singapore Closures

items.summary: The UK government announced a £100m investment to establish a new AI Biosecurity Lab, described as a world first, to strengthen defenses against biological threats. Supported by £200m in AI model credits from OpenAI and Anthropic, the initiative aims to safeguard national security and foster skilled jobs. Additional funding includes £120m for an AI Security Institute and £60m for a National Cyber Shield.
items.title: UK Announces £100m Investment in New AI Biosecurity Lab

items.summary: Producers of Blue Planet III deliberately included cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers the series is authentic. Executive producer Elizabeth White stated that the rise in AI makes them want to be even more authentic. Jack Bootle, the BBC's specialist factual commissioning head, assured journalists that no generative AI was used in the series. The show features novel animal behaviour captured using cutting-edge technology.
items.title: Blue Planet III Uses Cloudier Footage to Prove Authenticity Amid AI Boom

items.summary: The article introduces Quick Study, a project that rapidly paints a photo using a canvas element and simulated paintbrushes. It employs Sobel edge detection and relies solely on Google Fonts without external libraries. The post also lists recent articles, including updates on Battle Drones, Python versions, and Claude Haiku 5.5.
items.title: Quick Study: A Rapid Photo Painting Experiment

items.summary: Moonshot AI has released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3T-class open-weight model featuring 2.8T total and 104B active parameters with a 1M-token context window. The model is currently available via API but open weights are expected in November 2026. Self-reported benchmarks show it leads on SWE-Marathon at 51.7 but trails GPT-6 Astra on scientific tasks. It offers cheaper pricing than its predecessor K3, with input costs at $2.00 per million tokens. The model utilizes a Stable LatentMoE framework and runs on supernodes of 64+ accelerators.
items.title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K3.1 Pro with massive parameters and long context

items.summary: Eye Security researchers disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, which exposed millions of devices to remote code execution attacks. The flaw allowed attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on Windows and macOS systems. Researchers registered associated domains and delivered remediation code, reducing update requests by 98%, though Android users remain exposed.
items.title: Eye Security disables vulnerable updater in abandoned Time4Popcorn app

items.summary: Moonshot introduced the Kimi K3.1 Pro model on its API, promising full open weights by November 4, 2026. The model features a Highspeed version twice as fast at double the price. Benchmarks place it near the frontier, scoring 55 against models like Claude Opus 5.5. Pricing is $2.00 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
items.title: Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro with open weights promise

items.summary: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 will take place on November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston. Hosted by TechCrunch in partnership with Fidelity Private Shares, the event brings together founders, investors, and operators to discuss critical startup challenges. Sessions will cover scaling, product-market fit, building teams, and pitching. Speakers include Steve Fredette of Toast, Kent Bennett of Bessemer Venture Partners, and others. The agenda aims to move beyond fundraising and AI trends, focusing on practical strategies for building and scaling companies outside traditional hubs like Silicon Valley. Attendees can save 25% on tickets with a limited-time offer.
items.title: TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 to Explore Startup Growth Strategies in Boston

items.summary: Despite a tariff war between the United States and Canada, leaders have avoided taxing oil and gas due to deep energy interdependence. Canada supplies half of U.S. foreign petroleum imports, while 84% of Canadian oil and 76% of its electricity went to the U.S. in 2024. Experts note that untangling this integrated system would take decades and remain costly.
items.title: Trump and Carney Avoid Energy Tariffs Due to Deep North American Integration

items.summary: Robert Berke, writing for Oilprice.com, outlines a strategy attributed to President Trump to control global energy supplies while denying them to China. Following a phone call with President Putin, the Treasury Department issued a waiver allowing Russian diesel sales to lower fuel prices before the November 3 midterms. The author argues this move fits a broader pattern of isolating China, citing previous actions in Venezuela and Iran. The strategy involves potentially returning US oil companies to Russia and reviving Nord Stream pipelines to aid Europe. Berke suggests this approach mirrors Nixon's historical maneuvering but in reverse, aiming to pry Russia away from China. However, the plan faces opposition from President Zelensky and risks higher energy costs and inflation globally.
items.title: Trump's Energy Strategy to Isolate China and Aid Europe

items.summary: General Motors and Peak Energy are developing sodium-ion battery cells for grid-scale energy storage, not electric vehicles. GM Ventures invested in Peak Energy, which aims to reduce storage costs by 20% and achieve over 99% uptime. The partnership targets the growing market for stationary storage supporting renewable energy and data centers, utilizing a passively cooled platform that eliminates active cooling systems.
items.title: GM Partners With Peak Energy For Sodium-Ion Grid Storage

items.summary: Fenn Church, a homeowner in Calera, Alabama, successfully obtained a temporary injunction preventing Alabama Power from accessing his property to build a transmission line. However, the Alabama Supreme Court stayed the injunction, allowing the utility to proceed. Despite Church's efforts to mobilize support and the presence of allies like Rep. Phillip Ensler, Alabama Power crews bypassed the blockade by accessing the property through a rear route. Church vowed to continue resisting the utility's actions.
items.title: Homeowner Blocks Alabama Power Access to Property

items.summary: Boeing is demolishing five buildings at the former Santa Susana Field Laboratory in Southern California, raising concerns among nearby residents about potential cancer risks from plutonium-239. While state regulators and Boeing maintain the site poses no elevated risk and follows legal requirements, critics argue the original safety studies used outdated methods. Opponents, including Parents Against SSFL, dispute the premise that the buildings are uncontaminated, citing historical radiation readings and recent wind conditions that could spread dust. The site, once used for nuclear research, is slated to become a public recreation area despite fierce opposition.
items.title: Boeing Demolition at Santa Susana Lab Sparks Health Concerns

items.summary: Hyundai's larger IONIQ 9 electric SUV may offer a better lease deal than the popular IONIQ 5. While the IONIQ 5 starts at about $35,000, the IONIQ 9 begins at $58,955. However, a 36-month lease for the IONIQ 9 has an effective cost of $557 per month, which is only $7 higher than a 36-month lease for the IONIQ 5. The IONIQ 9 also provides three rows of seating and up to 335 miles of range.
items.title: Hyundai IONIQ 9 Lease May Outperform Smaller IONIQ 5 Sibling

items.summary: Influential environmental groups like the Natural Resources Defense Council and the Sierra Club oppose the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, fearing provisions on 'project certainty' will advantage fossil fuels over clean energy. While proponents argue the bill accelerates clean energy deployment, critics worry it creates legal shields for existing plants and limits state authority. Although independent analyses suggest net benefits for clean energy through 2041, advocates note the model may overlook unintended consequences like LNG export growth. As the Senate approaches a November 9 vote, the bill faces scrutiny from activists, state attorneys general, and tribal nations, with some centrist groups offering support despite these reservations.
items.title: Green Groups Withhold Support for Senate Permitting Deal Amid Concerns

items.summary: Rep. Rob Menendez introduced HR 10851, the 'Socket Full of Sunshine Act,' in the House on Oct. 19. The legislation seeks to legalize nationwide plug-in solar use by amending the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978. It would allow systems up to 1.2 kW without utility approval and create a grant program offering rebates of up to $1,000, provided 55% of components are U.S.-made. The bill also establishes safety standards and protects renters' rights to install such systems.
items.title: New Bill Aims to Legalize Nationwide Plug-in Solar Adoption

items.summary: A new report published in BioScience describes a bleak state of the planet's climate systems, noting that 16 examined indicators are worsening, with seven at record extremes. Authors William Ripple and Timothy Searchinger argue that human behavior, particularly meat consumption, drives these changes. Ripple states that shifting toward plant-based diets could make a meaningful difference, while Searchinger suggests Americans could help by eating fewer hamburgers. The report identifies ruminant livestock as a major source of methane and notes that reducing meat intake is an effective short-term tool to curb warming. The authors conclude that addressing global warming requires changing what people eat and how food is produced.
items.title: New Report Links Climate Crisis to Meat Consumption and Diet

items.summary: The Trump administration announced it would lift 50% tariffs on specific Canadian goods, including plywood and machinery, starting October 30. This move follows lobbying by Senator Susan Collins, who argued the exemptions would aid Maine's agriculture sector. While some tariffs are removed, others on carpets and waste products remain. The decision occurs two weeks before the US midterm elections, amidst ongoing trade tensions and Canadian countermeasures.
items.title: White House Lifts Some Canadian Tariffs Before Midterms

items.summary: The White House announced that President Trump removed certain tariffs on Canada to serve the public interest and assist Senator Susan Collins in her re-election campaign. The exemptions cover nine agricultural products and specific processing equipment crucial for Maine businesses. While Collins sought the relief, Democrats criticized the move as a desperate political maneuver. The decision occurs amidst a broader trade dispute where Canada has imposed retaliatory tariffs on American goods, causing significant drops in auto and other exports. Collins, who has frequently opposed Trump's trade policies, faces a tight race against Democrat Troy Jackson in a state considered pivotal for Congress.
items.title: Trump Eases Canada Tariffs to Aid Susan Collins in Maine

items.summary: The State Bank of India informed customers affected by a recent cyber incident that it contacted them via email and WhatsApp. The bank reiterated that account balances and funds remain safe. This update, shared on social media on October 23, followed an earlier post regarding the cybersecurity issue, confirming that affected individuals were notified individually.
items.title: SBI Notifies Customers of Cyber Incident and Reassures on Funds

items.summary: The article examines the UK state pension's competitiveness against other wealthy nations, noting that while the UK's basic state pension replacement rate is lower than the OECD average, the inclusion of occupational and personal pensions narrows this gap. Despite the generous triple lock formula, pensioner poverty has risen due to high housing costs. The UK faces a significant gender pension gap, with women receiving substantially less than men. Future reforms under Andy Burnham may reduce generosity but aim for sustainability amidst an ageing population and rising debt costs.
items.title: UK State Pension Comparison and Future Outlook

items.summary: Jio Platforms shares are trading with a grey market premium of approximately ₹238, or nearly 21% above the IPO price band, suggesting positive investor sentiment. This premium implies an estimated listing price of ₹1,357 per share compared to the issue price of ₹1,119. However, this figure remains an unofficial indicator of market mood and does not guarantee actual listing gains. Real demand will be confirmed when the shares debut on the BSE and NSE on October 28, 2026.
items.title: Jio Platforms Shares Command 21% Grey Market Premium Ahead of Debut

items.summary: Britain's government announced approximately £600 million in funding on Saturday to address AI-related health and security threats. The package includes a new biosecurity initiative, expanded cyber defenses, and support for AI research and robotics. AI Minister Kanishka Narayan stated the goal is to establish a global institution for protecting against emerging biological threats.
items.title: UK Government Announces £600 Million AI Security Funding Package

items.summary: Elizabeth Barron, director of the PHP Foundation, stated the organization is under-funded while managing critical security flaws. The foundation, which may support up to 70% of global sites, operates with one full-time staff member and 14 mostly part-time contractors. While AI aided in finding decade-old vulnerabilities, it also increased workloads. Barron noted the foundation relies on donations and grants to coordinate fixes with partners like OpenAI and Wiz.
items.title: PHP Foundation Director Says Organization Is Under-Funded Amid Security Crisis

items.summary: House Democrats are pursuing a competitive seat in Kansas, while Republicans aim to hold a California district. Democratic polling in Kansas shows a narrow lead for Democrats, whereas Republicans in California report a tight race. Both sides are releasing data to support their claims regarding these specific congressional seats.
items.title: Democrats Target Kansas Seat While Republicans Eye California District

items.summary: President Donald Trump's administration lifted certain tariffs on Canadian imports, including plywood and machinery, two weeks before the midterm elections. The White House stated the move follows lobbying by Senator Susan Collins, a vulnerable Republican in Maine. While easing levies on some goods, the administration imposed new ones on carpets and waste products, effective Oct 30. The action aims to assist Maine farmers reliant on Canadian equipment.
items.title: Trump Lifts Some Canada Tariffs Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: A CGTN poll indicates that over 60% of respondents believe China's Global Governance Initiative offers a path forward for inclusive global governance. The article argues that effective governance requires practical solutions to real-world problems like poverty and infrastructure, rather than empty rhetoric. It highlights the need for a system where every country has a voice and addresses shared challenges in technology and development.
items.title: CGTN Poll Finds Global Support for China's Governance Ideas

items.summary: Speaking at a gathering in Beijing on October 22, 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping highlighted the enduring relevance of the Long March spirit for China's modernization. Reflecting on the 1935 Zunyi Meeting, he emphasized the importance of Party leadership, independent innovation, and seeking truth from facts. Xi noted that while today's challenges differ from the revolutionary era, the principles of self-reliance and adapting to changing circumstances remain vital. He called for carrying forward the Long March spirit to address contemporary issues, including technological transformation and international landscape shifts, ensuring development benefits are shared equitably among the people.
items.title: Xi Jinping Draws Lessons from Long March for China's Modernization

items.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines's condition has been downgraded to serious but stable following an alleged attack near her electorate office in north-east Victoria. She lost both legs after being struck by a car. Surgeons attempted to save her right leg, but both had to be amputated due to the severity of her injuries. Police charged Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving and other offences. Haines's staff are working to reopen her offices.
items.title: MP Helen Haines Condition Downgraded After Alleged Attack

items.summary: A US envoy stated that Washington could strike Iran as soon as this weekend, citing mounting threats from both Washington and Israel. Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey, confirmed the possibility during an interview. While President Trump remains open to a deal, he previously indicated strikes would not occur before the Nov 3 US congressional elections. Barrack clarified that the US is not seeking regime change in Iran.
items.title: US Envoy Warns of Potential Strike on Iran This Weekend

items.summary: Esther Fischer, a 75-year-old retiree from Perth, became the world's oldest person to perform a handstand, smashing the previous record of 15 seconds with a 55-second hold. The 74-year-old American man previously held the record. Fischer, who started training at 65, now aims to become the oldest person to perform a one-arm handstand. Her achievement inspired her gym to introduce a longevity class for people aged 60 and over.
items.title: Perth woman sets world record as oldest person to do handstand

items.summary: Australian surfer Molly Picklum won the Rip Curl Pro in Portugal, securing the World Surf League title. She defeated American Caitlin Simmers in the final. Picklum now leads Carissa Moore in the standings with 48,950 points. The victory marks her first of the season at the Supertubos venue.
items.title: Molly Picklum Wins Rip Curl Pro to Lead WSL Standings

items.summary: Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence could trigger two decades of economic and social upheaval, even if the technology is managed successfully. Describing the timeframe as an estimate rather than a firm prediction, he noted that the transition would create winners and losers while reshaping employment and society. Gates urged stronger government oversight and technical safeguards, arguing that AI companies alone cannot manage the risks.
items.title: Bill Gates Warns of Two Decades of AI-Driven Turmoil

items.summary: Gora Kadan ryokan, established in 1948 in Hakone, recently expanded near Mount Fuji. Its president, Ryutaro Hashimoto, notes that while the market historically relied on domestic demand, inbound foreign tourists have surged from 8 million to 42 million over the last decade. Consequently, the inn is assessing whether the global market has an appetite for its luxury hospitality brand.
items.title: Gora Kadan Ryokan Expands and Questions Global Demand

items.summary: US President Donald Trump and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke by phone on Friday regarding the Russia-Ukraine war, the Middle East situation, and bilateral ties. They discussed Ukraine's access to Starlink technology, nuclear power collaboration, and the Jackdaw gas field approval. The leaders also addressed the Sea Lion project and Saudi Arabia's role in Yemen.
items.title: US President and UK Premier Discuss Ukraine War and Middle East

items.summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen attended a ceremony in Budapest to mark the 70th anniversary of the 1956 revolution. Magyar laid flowers at memorials, including that of Imre Nagy. The uprising lasted 15 days before Soviet forces crushed it, killing up to 3,000 revolutionaries. Von der Leyen praised the fighters' courage while noting Hungary's ongoing request for frozen EU funds.
items.title: Hungarian Leaders Honor 1956 Uprising Victims at Commemoration Ceremony

items.summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen attended a ceremony in Budapest to honor victims of the 1956 revolution. The uprising lasted 15 days and killed up to 3,000 revolutionaries before Soviet forces crushed it. While leaders praised the struggle for freedom, Hungary currently faces a challenge to unlock billions of euros in frozen EU funding due to rule-of-law concerns.
items.title: Hungarian Leaders Commemorate 1956 Uprising Victims Amid EU Funding Dispute

items.summary: Zambeze Delta Safaris, led by Mark Haldane, won the 2026 Markhor Award in Yerevan for restoring wildlife in Mozambique's Zambezi Delta. The operator combines regulated hunting with conservation. While Haldane credits the approach for population increases, Mongabay noted figures were not independently verified. The award highlights sustainable management amid global biodiversity concerns.
items.title: Mozambican Safari Operator Wins Conservation Award at COP17

items.summary: At the 46th Princess of Asturias Awards in Oviedo, laureates and dignitaries addressed contemporary disillusionment and the need for hope. The ceremony featured speeches by poet Patti Smith, historian Timothy Garton Ash, and engineer Christina Koch, who emphasized collectivity, European unity, and the value of human effort over artificial intelligence. King Felipe VI and the Princess of Asturias Foundation highlighted the importance of democracy and civic commitment. The event, held at the Campoamor Theatre, concluded with a quote from Paul Valéry delivered by the Princess, reinforcing the theme of resilience against darker times.
items.title: Princess of Asturias Laureates Address Disillusionment and Hope

items.summary: A criminal investigation into Argentine President Javier Milei and his sister regarding cryptocurrency links has been dismissed by federal judge Marcelo Martinez de Giorgi. Prosecutors requested the dismissal, and the judge concluded that no criminally relevant deception was proven. Milei previously denied promoting the collapsed $Libra coin, stating he acted in good faith and merely shared the link without promoting it.
items.title: Argentina Drops Investigation Into President Milei Over Crypto Fraud Allegations

items.summary: Men in Johannesburg participated in the Hollard Daredevil Race wearing purple swim briefs to raise awareness about prostate cancer, the most common cancer in South Africa. Organizer statements highlight that the topic is rarely discussed despite high risk. Participant Motaung Lehasa shared personal loss and emphasized the importance of attendance despite hot weather. Studies indicate low awareness and screening knowledge among Black men in the Free State and Limpopo provinces.
items.title: Johannesburg Men Run in Purple Briefs for Prostate Cancer Awareness

items.summary: Former Ukrainian prisoners Dmytro Khyliuk and Ihor Shyshko allege that Stephen Hubbard, a freed US citizen, was tortured in Russian custody. They claim he was beaten, humiliated, and subjected to harsh conditions including cold and lack of food. Hubbard was released after four-and-a-half years following a meeting between US envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin. While Hubbard's family confirmed the torture allegations, the International Committee of the Red Cross stated it requests to see every individual when granted access. Khyliuk described the treatment as a torture machine comparable to the Soviet regime.
items.title: Former Ukrainian Prisoners Allegate Torture of Freed US Citizen Stephen Hubbard in Russian Jail

items.summary: Russia is intensifying attacks on Kyiv, transforming the capital into a front-line city where residents face severe hardships. With insufficient shelters, subway stations serve as makeshift dormitories for the 4 million residents. Deaths rose to 140 in the first eight months of 2026, compared to 172 in all of 2025. Emergency power outages resumed, and the subway was paralyzed. Despite these challenges, 72% of residents remain prepared to endure the war. Authorities have adjusted curfews and allowed some facilities to operate during yellow alerts, though red alerts require immediate sheltering.
items.title: Russia Intensifies Attacks on Kyiv as Residents Face Harsh Conditions

items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that Tata Sons must list publicly while classified as an upper-layer NBFC due to systemic risks. This comment addresses doubts about a September order rejecting the company's deregistration request. Although the board agreed to comply with regulations, it has not yet decided on a market debut, with Noel Tata suggesting alternatives.
items.title: RBI Governor Says Tata Sons Must List As UL-NBFC

items.summary: An RBI study reveals that while India's non-banking financial companies expanded loan books and improved profitability in 2025, their share of the financial system slipped to 12.7 per cent from 13.9 per cent in 2020. Banks retained a dominant 52.3 per cent share. NBFCs remain a key credit source for underserved segments, with robust growth driven by secured lending and retail loans, though dependence on external borrowing remains a concern requiring monitoring.
items.title: RBI Study Shows NBFCs Losing Ground Despite Stronger Profitability

items.summary: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav handed over letters of intent for office space to seven companies at Indore's IT Park-4. The projects are expected to generate 1,280 direct jobs and involve a combined 44,815.67 sq ft of space. Separately, five companies received land allotment LoIs for industrial projects with proposed investments of Rs 9,625 crore and over 4,450 direct jobs across Bhopal, Indore, and Gwalior.
items.title: MP Chief Minister hands over IT Park-4 space to seven semiconductor firms

items.summary: The Trump administration has eased tariffs on specific Canadian imports, including plywood and machinery, two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. White House officials stated the changes target products vital to Maine's agricultural sector. Senator Susan Collins secured these exemptions for her state, though new duties on other goods like carpets will remain in effect starting October 30.
items.title: Trump Administration Eases Tariffs on Canadian Imports Ahead of Midterms

items.summary: Microsoft researchers developed an AI tool that diagnoses patients sequentially, coordinating questions and tests like a doctor. According to a study in Science, this model was more than twice as accurate as general physicians on complex cases. The tool outperformed human doctors in emergency scenarios and reduced diagnostic costs. Researchers plan to test its triage abilities in Boston emergency departments.
items.title: Microsoft AI Tool Diagnoses Patients Sequentially Like Doctors

items.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar visited Baku to reset ties with Azerbaijan following friction over Operation Sindoor. The two leaders agreed to expand cooperation in energy, trade, and connectivity. Jaishankar noted this was the first visit by an Indian foreign minister in eight years, building on goodwill from PM Modi's recent meeting with Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev. They discussed terrorism and welcomed a peace agreement between Azerbaijan and Armenia.
items.title: India and Azerbaijan Reset Ties After Operation Sindoor Friction

items.summary: A study published in Atmospheric Pollution Research found that the 2022-23 La Niña winter brought cleaner air to north India, with PM2.5 levels down by up to 30%, while peninsular India saw spikes. The following El Niño winter reversed this pattern, causing pollution to accumulate in the north and disperse in the south. Researchers caution that these findings are based on two unique years and do not establish direct causation for future winters.
items.title: Study traces how El Niño changed India's pollution map

items.summary: Shriram Finance reported a 59% year-on-year profit increase to Rs 3,677 crore, driven by strong interest income and lower funding costs. Net interest margin improved to 9.52% from 8.19%. MD & CEO Parag Sharma expects the margin to remain around 9% for the next two quarters before returning to the 8.5% long-term guidance level.
items.title: Shriram Finance Reports 59% Profit Jump on Strong Interest Income

items.summary: BPCL reported a 21% year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs 4,863 crore for Q2, while revenue from operations rose 29.78% to Rs 1,57,817.93 crore. Total expenses increased 32.54% to Rs 1,51,932.8 crore. The company's board approved a subsidiary for a greenfield refinery in Ramayapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, with authorized capital up to Rs 4,900 crore, pending regulatory approvals.
items.title: BPCL Reports Q2 Profit Decline Amid Revenue Growth and Refinery Expansion Plans

items.summary: Seven people were killed and 40 wounded when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, authorities said. Footage showed multiple assailants shooting before fleeing. Jordan declared three days of national mourning. King Abdullah II condemned the terrorist act, while regional leaders and the UN expressed solidarity and called for accountability.
items.title: Seven Killed in Gun Attack on Church in Jordan

items.summary: A fire at Bhopal's Adampur dumping site was controlled in 30 minutes, reigniting concerns over recurring incidents and air pollution affecting nearby residents. The Bhopal Municipal Corporation faces a Supreme Court deadline of March 31, 2027, to clear 6.5 lakh metric tonnes of legacy waste. Officials have awarded a Rs 52 crore contract to Saurashtra Company for the operation, though management challenges persist.
items.title: Bhopal Adampur Dumping Site Fire Raises Concerns Over Legacy Waste Clearance Deadline

items.summary: Police in Chhattisgarh arrested Mayur Meshram for allegedly pushing his wife, Neelam, into the Mohara river after repeated marital disputes. The incident occurred on October 21 in Rajnandgaon district, where Meshram took his non-swimming wife on a pretext of an outing. Following the altercation, she drowned. Meshram confessed to his brother-in-law and was subsequently arrested and sent to jail on October 22.
items.title: Chhattisgarh Man Pushes Wife Into River Over Marital Disputes

items.summary: Indian-origin candidates are contesting various offices in the November 3, 2026, US midterm elections, including the US House, state legislatures, and gubernatorial races. Notable contenders include Republican Vivek Ramaswamy seeking the Ohio governorship and Democrats Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera, and Suhas Subramanyam seeking re-election to Congress. Races span states like California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York, and Maryland. The elections will determine party control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term, with Republicans currently holding both chambers.
items.title: Indian-Origin Candidates Seek Office in 2026 US Midterms

items.summary: The Indian government told the Supreme Court that hospitals impose steep markups on medicines and consumables, describing the practice as malpractice due to patients' low bargaining power. The Centre proposed capping trade margins on non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines at 30%, a move it said could reduce prices by 20% to 70% and save patients around Rs 2,500 crore annually. While the government argued competition alone could not address pricing concerns due to information asymmetries, the Supreme Court questioned why measures were limited to cancer drugs and urged a broader examination of drug pricing practices. The Centre stated it is consulting stakeholders to address the issue.
items.title: Centre Proposes Margin Cap on Cancer Drugs Amid Hospital Malpractice Allegations

items.summary: Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, on Friday, killing seven people and injuring 34. Authorities described the attackers as unknown assailants and stated investigations are underway. King Abdullah II condemned the act and vowed a strong response, while regional leaders offered condolences. The attack has renewed attention on Karak's history of violence.
items.title: Gunmen Kill 7, Wound 34 During Funeral Attack in Jordan
